title: Helping the Needy
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child states why Christians help the needy (love for God and neighbour; Matthew 5:42), names ways to help that are not money (sharing food, carrying a load, visiting), and knows anyone can help.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the Good Samaritan helped a stranger.
floor.question: Who stopped to help the hurt man?

representations: a ladder of help: notice, care, act
steps: Help now, with what you have.
Help out of love, not for praise.

board.do: Write Matthew 5:42: "Give to the one who asks you".
Point at the picture of a child with no lunch.
board.say: How can you help even without money?

board.do: Wait for the child to name a way.
List the ways on the board.

misconceptions.ask: Who can help someone in need?
misconceptions.repair: List what a child with no money can give: time, a pencil, a kind word.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a way of helping a person in need?
misconceptions.repair: Make a list of ways to help at home, school and church.

listen_for: So that people will praise me
misconceptions.ask: Why should a Christian help the needy?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether Jesus helped for praise.

listen_for: Help after the test if I remember
misconceptions.ask: A classmate has no pencil for the test and asks you. What does Matthew 5:42 teach?
misconceptions.repair: Act it: the test starts now. Help that comes later is no help.

checks.question: Can a child without money help a needy person?
checks.answer: Yes: share food, carry a load, visit

checks.question: Why does a Christian help the needy?
checks.answer: Out of love for God and others
